How tm8 is built · identity & action

Who gets to act

A Server begins with one claim, admits people by invitation, and gives a running session exactly one teammate identity. Drive the ledger to see each actor enter the graph.

Plate 1 · Before identity Unclaimed
I · Claim · status

The node answers first

auth claim status is deliberately readable without credentials. The answer is about the Server, not a browser’s memory.

Illustrative one-time claim token tm8c_R7A3…C91K
on-box only
Why rotation matterstm8 auth claim reissue writes a fresh token to <dataDir>/setup-token with mode 0600 and invalidates the previous token. It refuses after the node is claimed.
I · Claim · credential

Claiming preserves the owner

The token authorizes one first-run ceremony. tm8 sets a password on the existing owner account, burns the token, and signs the caller in.

Attribution stays putRows created by the loopback auto-owner keep the same identity. Claim is not a second owner and it is not open signup.
server host · claimCLI
tm8 auth claim --token <tm8c_…> --username mara --password <password>
claimed this Server as Mara Voss (@mara)
the claim token is now burned — this node cannot be claimed again
II · Invite · preview

Read the invitation before joining

The code is the authorization. space invite resolve takes no Space id; a valid code says what it joins and which non-owner role it confers.

Disclosure is narrowAn unknown code reveals nothing. Expired, revoked, or exhausted codes may name the Space, but never the inviter.
invitee shell · previewCLI
tm8 space invite resolve <inv_…>
valid  space Northlake  join as member  invited by Mara Voss  expires never
II · Invite · redeem

The invitee chooses the password

One transaction creates Theo’s account and member row, consumes the invite, and signs Theo in. No input can make this account a node admin or Space owner.

Operator · Mara

Creates an invite and sends the code out of band. not known

Invitee · Theo

Picks a password in the redeeming request. ••••••••••
Redeem and sign in tm8 auth invite signup --code <inv_…> --username theo --password <password> → joined space <space-id> as Theo Iwu (@theo)
Transport boundaryThe password travels in the request body; a real remote deployment needs TLS. The operator never receives it.
III · Session · persona

A teammate is who

JUJuniperteam_member is a durable agent persona and a first-class graph actor. It does not run by itself.

Shape carries meaningCircle means a human member. Rounded square means an agent team_member. Both can author graph work.
Northlake · launchCLI
tm8 session spawn --space <space-id> --teammate <team-member-id> --task <task-id> --workdir worktree
A session runs one teammate persona; its workdir is Server-computed.
III · Session · action

A session is now

The Server starts a real PTY and gives it a bearer session whose actingAsTeamMemberId names Juniper. The process writes as that teammate—not as the human who launched it.

One persona per agent sessionThe work session is the running container, not an actor disguise. Its credential resolves every permitted mutation to one team_member.
Juniper · work sessionPTY
tm8 message send --to <task-id> "Claim path verified."
batch <message-batch-id>
<message-id>
Northlake · actor ledgersolid ink = shipped
No credential yet. The Server exposes only the bootstrap status and waits for its one-time claim token.

04The boundaries are part of the model

No open signup

Admission is deliberate

auth signup is node-admin-only. Everyone else enters a claimed node with an invite code.

Change ≠ reset

No password reset

auth password requires the current password. tm8 has no reset-without-the-old-password path.

One resolved actor

Sessions carry identity

A session minted for a teammate resolves its permitted mutations to that one team_member.
